replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Not really. I’ve never felt anxious about math because I’ve used it practically for things like budgeting and baking. My parents’ higher education helped me understand it better, and I focus on real-world applications rather than abstract concepts.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: I used a simple math app for budgeting last year. It helped me track expenses and calculate percentages, but I didn’t use it for advanced topics. I prefer hands-on practice over AI tools for learning math.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form ax² + bx + c = 0. Then, calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac). If it’s positive, you get two real solutions. Use the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(discriminant)] / (2a). This method works for any second-order equation.

To find stationary points, take the first derivative f'(x). Set it equal to zero and solve for x. These x-values are critical points. Then plug them back into f(x) to find the corresponding y-values. These points are where the graph might change direction.
